title: Handle late and duplicate events with a watermark
prompt: The hourly activity board can't wait forever for stragglers. The team's policy: wait two hours of event time, then publish the hour and drop anything older. Write `hourly_counts(events)`, the watermark policy, which `run_hourly` (given) runs with `foreachBatch`. Then write `batch_timeline(page_views, cart_events, checkout_events)`: one row per micro-batch from the query's progress reports, so the watermark can be watched at work.
rules: `hourly_counts` takes the event stream, puts a 2-hour watermark on `event_time`, drops repeated deliveries (same `event_id`) with `dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark`, and counts the events in each 1-hour window of `event_time`. It returns `window_start` and `events`.

`batch_timeline` runs `run_hourly` on `event_stream(...)` with a fresh checkpoint and returns one row per micro-batch, from the reports in the query's `recentProgress`, skipping any report with no state operators (Spark posts one when a run finds nothing to read): `micro_batch` (`batchId`), `input_rows` (`numInputRows`) and `watermark`, the report's `eventTime["watermark"]` as text: its first 19 characters, with the `T` replaced by a space.

Each report lists two state operators, told apart by `operatorName`: the duplicate check (`dedupeWithinWatermark`) and the hourly count (`stateStoreSave`). `late_rows_dropped` is the sum of their `numRowsDroppedByWatermark`; `ids_in_state` and `hours_in_state` are their `numRowsTotal`.
`hours_published` is how many rows `run_hourly` published in that micro-batch and `events_published` the sum of their `events`, both 0 when it published nothing.
hints: `events.withWatermark("event_time", "2 hours").dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark(["event_id"])`, then `groupBy(F.window("event_time", "1 hour"))`. `F.col("window.start")` is the window's start.

Clear the checkpoint, then `q, published = run_hourly(stream, checkpoint)`. Read each report in `q.recentProgress` like a dict: `p["eventTime"]["watermark"]`, `p["stateOperators"]`. A dict by name, `{o["operatorName"]: o for o in p["stateOperators"]}`, finds each operator.

Append mode publishes an hour only once the watermark reaches its end, so the last micro-batch reads nothing: it runs because the watermark moved. A row is late, and dropped, when it is at or before the previous micro-batch's watermark.
explanation: The watermark is the stream's promise about lateness: two hours behind the latest event time seen. Spark computes it at the end of each micro-batch and drops a row as late when it is at or before the previous micro-batch's watermark, so a straggler that arrives just one delivery later still counts, and only rows older than that are dropped. `dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark` remembers each `event_id` only until the watermark passes its event time plus two hours, so its state shrinks instead of growing forever. The timeline makes all of this visible from stable progress fields: the watermark climbing, rows dropped, state rising and falling, and hours published once the watermark passes their end, including the last, data-free micro-batch that `availableNow` runs to move the watermark on.
